sisterShips: Carnival Adventure (ex Golden Princess, ex Pacific Adventure)
Carnival Encounter (ex Star Princess, ex Pacific Encounter)

zones.what: Lifeboats and tender boats are mounted on Deck 8 (Emerald), and Princess's own category codes OV, OW, OY and OZ mark the oceanview cabins on that deck as partially or fully blocked by them.
zones.effect: Guests in these Emerald-deck oceanview categories look at a lifeboat hull instead of open sea; some cabins between boats keep a partial view.
zones.mattersTo: View-focused oceanview bookers should avoid U-Z coded cabins unless discounted; sunlight-only seekers or budget cruisers who don't care about a clear sightline can take the savings
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Grand Princess Emerald deck page: 'Category OV, OW, OY, OZ have obstructed views'; corroborated by cruisemummy.co.uk and a Cruise Critic member cabin review describing an OW cabin as 'about 3/4 clear of obstructions'

zones.what: Deck 12 (Aloha) sits one physical deck directly below Deck 14 (Lido), since the ship's numbering skips deck 13.
zones.effect: Guests hear early-morning deck-chair scraping and late-night pool-deck cleaning through the ceiling, and must walk to the fore or aft stairs/lifts to reach the pool one level up.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and late-risers should avoid Aloha-deck mid cabins; pool-deck convenience seekers may still prefer it despite the noise
zones.source: cruiseaddicts.com Grand Princess forum: a guest reports their 'stateroom was mid-ship on the Aloha deck (one below Lido)' and found it inconvenient to reach the pool; corroborated independently by cruisemummy.co.uk's account of a guest credited on-board spend after complaining about pool-deck scraping noise

zones.what: Certain Emerald-deck (8) cabins sit directly over the stage of the Explorer's Lounge / Club Fusion nightspot.
zones.effect: When the band plays, the floor and furniture vibrate with the drumbeat, and the venue runs until nearly midnight.
zones.mattersTo: Anyone wanting an early, quiet night should avoid this stack; nightlife-adjacent guests may not mind
zones.source: Cruise Critic member review of Grand Princess cabin E516: 'directly over the stage of the Explorer's Lounge... floor and chairs vibrate with each drumbeat... party down below lasts until about 11:40 pm'; cruisedeckplans.com Emerald deck notes separately warn to 'avoid cabins above Club Fusion and Explorers Lounge'

zones.what: Forward Emerald-deck (8) cabins sit above and/or below the main Princess Theater, and above a crew work area.
zones.effect: Stage-production show noise and rehearsal sound can carry into these cabins, plus occasional crew-area noise.
zones.mattersTo: Show-noise-sensitive guests should avoid forward Emerald cabins; theater-goers who like proximity may not mind the short walk
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Grand Princess Emerald deck page: 'Forward cabins on this deck are above or below the main theater and may have noise' and 'Forward cabins are above crew area and may have noise at times'

zones.what: The seven Suite-category cabins added to Deck 6 (Fiesta) in the 2011 refurbishment sit near the casino and entertainment lounges.
zones.effect: Late-night casino and lounge traffic/noise reaches these suites more than other suite locations on the ship.
zones.mattersTo: Suite guests wanting quiet evenings should ask for a different suite deck; guests who enjoy being near the action may like it
zones.source: Cruise Critic Grand Princess cabins editorial: 'The newest were added on Deck 6, near the casino, during the 2011 refurbishment'

zones.what: On Grand Princess the midship passenger staircase does not continue above Deck 7, unlike the forward and aft staircases.
zones.effect: Guests in midship cabins on higher decks must wait for an elevator or walk to the fore/aft stairwells to change decks, which can mean 5-10 minute elevator waits at busy times.
zones.mattersTo: Guests who dislike elevator waits or want quick stair access should book near the forward or aft stairs, not midship on the upper decks
zones.source: Cruise Critic member review of Grand Princess: 'the Grand Princess has no passenger staircase midship above deck 7, you must either wait for an elevator... or walk to the forward or aft lift/staircases'

zones.what: The forward staircase on Grand Princess is reserved for crew, not passengers.
zones.effect: Guests near the forward stairwell can hear crew moving between decks early in the morning as they prepare the ship for the day.
zones.mattersTo: Very light sleepers who want a lie-in should avoid cabins near the forward stairwell; most guests find this a minor, occasional issue
zones.source: cruisemummy.co.uk Grand Princess guide: 'The staircase at the front of the ship is for crew only, and some guests have reported that there can be some noise early in the morning when the crew are moving around'

zones.what: There is a crew work area on Dolphin deck (9) near cabin D123, distinct from the surrounding all-cabin stretch of that deck.
zones.effect: Cabins immediately around this blank/crew space pick up service noise that neighboring all-passenger stretches of the deck do not.
zones.mattersTo: Noise-sensitive guests booking Dolphin deck should avoid the D123 vicinity; the rest of the deck is unusually quiet because it's sandwiched between all-cabin decks
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Grand Princess Dolphin deck page: 'Avoid cabins around blank space near D123. This is a crew area and may have noise'

zones.what: Guests on a dedicated Grand Princess forum thread report that most of the ship's noise and vibration is concentrated aft.
zones.effect: Aft cabins feel engine/propulsion vibration more than midship cabins on the same deck.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive sleepers should choose midship over aft; wake-view lovers may accept the trade-off
zones.source: cruiseaddicts.com thread 'Best Rooms with Less Movement/GRAND PRINCESS': 'Most of the noise and vibration is in the aft, and the worst movement is at the bow'

zones.what: The same Grand Princess-specific forum thread identifies the bow/forward area as where motion is worst.
zones.effect: Forward cabins, especially on higher decks, pitch and roll more in rough seas than midship cabins.
zones.mattersTo: First-time cruisers or those prone to seasickness should pick a low, midship, inside or oceanview cabin; motion-tolerant guests can enjoy the forward view
zones.source: cruiseaddicts.com Grand Princess forum: 'the closer to the center of gravity you are, the less movement you will feel... the worst movement is at the bow'

zones.what: Grand Princess balconies are tiered/stepped outward as you go down the hull, so each lower deck's balcony floor extends further out than the deck above it.
zones.effect: Passengers on a higher deck can look down onto the balconies of the deck immediately below them, reducing privacy for the lower cabin.
zones.mattersTo: Privacy-conscious sunbathers should book the topmost balcony deck available or a covered aft mini-suite; guests unconcerned about being seen from above can ignore this
zones.source: Cruise Critic Grand Princess cabins editorial: 'verandas are tiered, growing larger the lower on the ship you go... passengers with balconies on upper decks can see onto the balconies of those below them, leaving little privacy'; corroborated by a Grand Princess-specific cruiseaddicts.com thread

zones.what: A small number of aft mini-suites on Emerald deck (8), including E728 and E729, have a full covered/overhung balcony rather than the open tiered style.
zones.effect: These specific cabins escape the look-down privacy loss that affects most tiered balconies on the class, at the cost of full sun exposure.
zones.mattersTo: Guests who want balcony privacy over tanning should target these specific cabins; sun-worshippers should avoid them
zones.source: cruisedeckplans.com Grand Princess Emerald deck page: 'Aft Mini-Suites also have covered balconies (protection from rain and private from cabins above)... Mini-Suites E728 and E729 have extra large covered balcony'

zones.what: BF-category forward balcony cabins on Emerald deck (8) sit inboard where the hull steps up toward the bow, directly beside the transition stairs from the Promenade deck.
zones.effect: These balconies are fully covered (little sun), do not look straight out over the open sea because they are set back from the hull edge, and lack privacy because passengers climbing the stairway to the bow pass right by them.
zones.mattersTo: Guests wanting an open sea view or balcony privacy should avoid this specific BF forward category; bargain-hunters who just want outdoor space may be fine with it
zones.source: cruiseaddicts.com Grand Princess balcony thread: the BF forward cabins have a balcony that 'doesn't look down over the ocean, as it is fairly far inboard... sits out along the little section of the promenade where it transitions up... a pretty significant lack of privacy'

zones.what: Caribe deck (10) balconies are markedly larger than the standard tiered balconies on other decks, and are about half covered, half open.
zones.effect: Guests get a bigger outdoor space with some sun and some shade/privacy, widely called the 'best of both worlds' by repeat cruisers.
zones.mattersTo: Balcony-space seekers should target Caribe deck; budget cruisers indifferent to balcony size can ignore this
zones.source: cruiseaddicts.com Grand Princess balcony thread: 'the Caribe Deck is the way to go... Huge balcony and somewhat private'; corroborated by a Fodor's Grand Princess thread giving Caribe balcony dimensions as 9ft x 10ft

zones.what: Unlike her Grand-class sister ships, Grand Princess had her elevated aft Skywalkers-style nightclub removed in the 2011 refit because the top-heavy structure caused the ship to sail bow-up and hurt fuel efficiency.
zones.effect: High-deck aft cabins on Grand Princess do not sit under a late-night nightclub/observation lounge the way equivalent cabins do on sister ships that retain the structure.
zones.mattersTo: Aft-cabin bookers comparing Grand Princess to her sisters should know this specific noise source is absent on Grand Princess; nightlife fans who liked the Skywalkers vibe on sister ships won't find it here
zones.source: Wikipedia (Grand Princess): 'The aft nightclub atop the aft of Grand Princess was removed in the 2011 refit'; Travel Weekly's Skywalkers feature explains it 'had to be removed from the Grand Princess because it caused the ship to sail bow-up, reducing fuel efficiency'

zones.what: Grand Princess has Family Suites on Dolphin deck (9), specifically D105/D101 and D106/D102, sold as interconnecting staterooms sharing a private balcony and accommodating up to 8 guests.
zones.effect: These connecting-cabin sets let large family groups book adjoining rooms, but also mean noise/activity from one side is easily heard through the connecting door.
zones.mattersTo: Large families/groups wanting adjoining rooms should look here; guests wanting isolation from neighboring strangers should avoid connecting-door categories generally
zones.source: cruiseline.com Grand Princess deck plan notes: 'Family Suites D105/D101 & D106/D102 are interconnecting staterooms with private balcony; accommodates up to 8 people'
